title: Sola, sola in bujo loco
subtitle: Donna Elvira, Leporello, Donna Anna, Don Ottavio, Zerlina and Masetto: sextet from Don Giovanni, Act 2 (No. 19)

passages.label: Sola, sola in bujo loco · Più che cerco, men ritrovo · ecco il tempo di fuggir
Tergi il ciglio, o vita mia (D major)
Lascia almen alla mia pena · il mio pianto può finir
Ah dov' è lo sposo mio? · Una porta la vegg' io · Ferma, briccone! · Ah, mora il perfido! · O mio marito!
È Donna Elvira? · Appena il credo · No, no, morrà! · Pietà!
Perdon, perdono! · Quello io non sono · Viver lasciatemi per carità
Dei! Leporello? · Stupida resto! · Che mai sarrà (to the fermata)

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527 (1787), Act 2 scenes 7–8, No. 19 Sextet, from the beginning to the fermata before the Molto allegro
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Lorenzo Da Ponte, libretto of Don Giovanni (1787)
licences.author: Lorenzo Da Ponte (1749–1838)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score, which differ from the libretto in places: bujo (libretto buio); Ottavio dà and omai; Anna piccolo (some librettos picciolo); Elvira O mio marito! (libretto È mio marito); Elvira cheto, as Leporello (libretto cheta); Una porta la vegg' io, la without its accent; Perdon, perdono! Signori miei!; quà; stupida (the women) and stupido (Ottavio, Masetto); sarà printed sar-rà, so the word is written sarrà.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 188–199, bars 1–130 of No. 19 (to the fermata before the Molto allegro)
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages in three chunks (pp. 188–191, 192–195, 196–199): the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers, whose findings were corrected; the left hand of bar 1 starts in the treble clef, as printed. Don Ottavio's part, printed in the treble clef, is written at sounding pitch. Kept as printed: Donna Anna's A-flats in bars 81 and 83 (no natural printed) and the piano's E natural in bar 71 (the natural is missing in the print; the bar is a C major arpeggio). The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. The sextet goes on with the Molto allegro, "Mille torbidi pensieri", a separate piece. Playback tempo: ♩ = 100, about 5¼ minutes, the median (5:12) of five recordings that put the Andante on its own track or tracks, apart from the Molto allegro (Norrington 4:38, Haitink 1984 4:58, Busch 1936 5:12, Keilberth 1962 5:20, I. Fischer 5:23); Mozart gives the word Andante only.
